disclaimer: Compiled from news reports and public sources. Cases are allegations unless a court has ruled. Not legal advice; verify with a property lawyer.

scam_patterns.title: Same flat sold to multiple buyers
scam_patterns.how_it_works: A builder, agent or fake owner takes booking money or registers agreements for one flat with two or more buyers. Often the first buyer has only an allotment letter, not a registered agreement.
red_flags: Only an allotment letter or receipt offered, no registered agreement for sale
Pressure to pay large amounts in cash or to a personal account
Price noticeably below nearby flats with an urgency story
Builder refuses to show the flat on the MahaRERA inventory or the sold-unit list
prevention_checks: Search IGR Maharashtra (Index II / e-search) for any earlier registered document on the same flat
Register the agreement for sale promptly; pay stamp duty in your name
Pay only to the project's RERA designated bank account (new projects) or the registered owner's account (resale)
Ask the society secretary in writing whether anyone else has claimed the flat

recent_cases.summary: Two buyers allegedly paid for the same flat; the flat also had an existing loan.
Builder father and son arrested for allegedly selling the same flat to multiple buyers.
Developer directors booked for alleged fake flat promises and resale of the same flat to others.
Developer booked after a stalled project; a buyer found his booked flat was sold to someone else. Losses estimated above Rs 100 crore.

scam_patterns.title: Fake owner / fake online listing (resale)
scam_patterns.how_it_works: Fraudsters post a real flat on property portals, show it, and impersonate the owner with forged Aadhaar/PAN. They collect token and part payments, then disappear.
red_flags: Owner unavailable except through one 'broker'
Owner name on ID does not match Index II, share certificate or electricity bill
Urgent sale story (moving abroad, medical emergency) and below-market price
Request to pay token by UPI to a third party
prevention_checks: Match the seller's ID with the share certificate, Index II and society records in person
Meet the seller at the society office; get the secretary to confirm identity
Pay token only by cheque/transfer to the owner's own account, against a written receipt
Have a lawyer do a title search before paying more than a small token

recent_cases.summary: Police arrested six people who posted fake listings and used an impersonator with forged IDs as the owner.
A buyer paid part of the price to a fake owner and broker; the flat belonged to someone else.

scam_patterns.title: Undisclosed loan or charge on the flat
scam_patterns.how_it_works: The seller hides an existing home loan or mortgage. Original documents sit with a lender and the buyer cannot get clear title.
red_flags: Seller has only photocopies of the chain documents
Seller avoids giving a bank's list of documents or foreclosure letter
Society records show a lien on the share certificate
prevention_checks: Search CERSAI for registered charges on the property
Ask the society for its lien register and NOC
If a loan exists, pay the outstanding directly to the seller's bank and collect originals + closure letter

recent_cases.summary: Buyer alleges the sellers hid a loan on the flat; police registered a cheating case.

scam_patterns.title: Illegal building with forged CC/OC or RERA registration
scam_patterns.how_it_works: Buildings are put up on reserved or unapproved land with forged commencement/occupancy certificates. Some even got MahaRERA registration using fake papers. Courts have ordered demolitions, leaving buyers homeless.
red_flags: Price far below the area rate for a 'new' building
Builder cannot show CC/OC on the municipal portal, only paper copies
Land is on a development-plan reservation (garden, STP, dumping ground)
Many banks refuse to lend on the project
prevention_checks: Verify CC/OC number directly with the municipal corporation (e.g. VVCMC approved building list)
Check the development plan reservation for the survey number
Do not rely on RERA registration alone
Prefer projects where a major bank has approved project finance

recent_cases.summary: 41 illegal buildings on land reserved for a sewage plant and dumping ground were demolished on court orders; about 2,500 families displaced. ED probe ongoing.
Police probed 55 buildings built with forged documents and sold to about 3,500 families; some had RERA registration.
Two builders arrested for an eight-storey building allegedly built on a fake CC; 113 flats sold.
Bombay HC refused relief to an illegal building despite RERA registration; KDMC began action on 65 illegal buildings.

scam_patterns.title: SRA / redevelopment sale-component fraud
scam_patterns.how_it_works: In SRA or society redevelopment projects, the developer sells free-sale flats, diverts funds, or sells flats reserved for existing members. If the developer is replaced, earlier buyers may be left out of the new project.
red_flags: Developer cannot show the development agreement or SRA Letter of Intent
Flat number appears in the rehab or member allotment list
Project stalled for years or developer changed
Court order restraining third-party rights on the project
prevention_checks: Get the development agreement; confirm who has the right to sell which component
Check SRA / MHADA approvals and court cases on the project
Read MahaRERA project page for complaints, revised dates and quarterly updates
Pay only into the RERA designated account

recent_cases.summary: EOW arrested a builder over alleged fraud in an SRA project where sale money should have gone to a joint RERA account.
EOW case against nine people for allegedly cheating over 200 buyers in an SRA project.
After SRA replaced a defaulting developer, MahaRERA let the new developer start fresh; earlier buyers were left chasing refunds.
A redevelopment flat sold to a buyer was allegedly reserved for an original member and under a court restraint.

scam_patterns.title: Fake MHADA / MMRDA / government scheme flats
scam_patterns.how_it_works: Fraudsters pose as officials or agents and promise cheap MHADA, MMRDA or rehabilitation flats outside the official lottery, collecting fees and advances.
red_flags: Flat 'quota' or 'direct allotment' outside the official lottery
Price far below market
Payments to personal accounts or cash
prevention_checks: MHADA allots through its official lottery website only
Never pay an agent for allotment
Rehab flats generally cannot be sold for a lock-in period; verify transfer eligibility

recent_cases.summary: Scammers posing as MHADA officials allegedly cheated 61 people with promises of subsidised flats.
Two women booked for allegedly selling fake MMRDA rehabilitation flats to 15 buyers.

scam_patterns.title: Fake 'bank-seized' or auction flats
scam_patterns.how_it_works: Fraudsters offer discounted flats claimed to be seized by banks and take advances outside the bank's official auction process.
red_flags: Deal not listed on the bank's or e-auction portal
Payment asked to an individual
prevention_checks: Buy bank-auction property only through the bank's official SARFAESI auction notice and portal

recent_cases.summary: Four people allegedly paid for discounted 'bank-seized' flats that were never delivered.

scam_patterns.title: Forged sale deed / identity theft of owner
scam_patterns.how_it_works: Fraudsters forge the owner's photo and signature on a sale deed, using genuine ID copies, to sell the flat or raise loans on it.
red_flags: Recent registered transfer the society is unaware of
Board resolutions or POAs with discrepancies
prevention_checks: Cross-check the latest Index II with the society share register
Verify any power of attorney is registered and still valid

recent_cases.summary: A flat already sold in 2020 was allegedly 'sold' again in 2024 using forged documents and fake board resolutions.
An owner's identity was allegedly forged to raise a large bank loan against his flat.

scam_patterns.title: Delayed or stalled under-construction project
scam_patterns.how_it_works: Not always fraud: funds are diverted or the developer runs short, and possession slips by years. Buyers keep paying EMIs and rent.
red_flags: Possession date revised more than once on MahaRERA
Construction progress far behind the payment schedule
Many MahaRERA complaints against the developer
prevention_checks: Read the project's MahaRERA quarterly progress reports
Link payments to construction stages, not time
Check developer's track record of delivering past projects with OC

recent_cases.summary: MahaRERA acted again against a Mumbai builder over defects, delays and pending conveyance.

area_notes.area: Western & central suburbs SRA pockets (Jogeshwari, Borivali, Kurla, Goregaon, Bandra East, Mulund)
area_notes.note: Check development agreement and SRA approvals for sale-component flats.

general_precautions: Never pay more than a small token before a lawyer's title search
Pay only by traceable bank transfer to the right account; no cash component
Register the agreement for sale; an allotment letter alone gives weak protection
Check MahaRERA, IGR Index II, CERSAI and society records independently
Visit the site and society office yourself; talk to neighbours
Treat a deal far below market as a warning, not a bargain
